title: Compact Reserve Controller: autoscale & isolation PRD
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Enable a lightweight controller (Compact Reserve Controller) that coordinates reserved pool headroom, tenant burst allowances, and graceful fallback so Dedicated tenants receive predictable capacity while the system preserves overall SLOs.
problem_statement: Current reserved pools are static and either over-provision or cause caller-facing throttling during short bursts. There is no small-footprint control loop that enforces tenant isolation while allowing safe transient bursting and fast autoscale reactions for Dedicated capacity.
goals: Provide a low-latency control loop to allocate soft headroom from a shared reservoir to tenants during short bursts (minute-scale)
Enforce tenant isolation so misuse by one tenant cannot degrade other tenants beyond defined SLA windows
Support configurable burst budgets and decay (credits) per-tenant and per-reservation
Expose operator-safe controls and telemetry in Console for reserve state, reclaimed events, and fallback activations
non_goals: Replacing long-term economic reservation contracts or billing model changes
Full rewrite of Dedicated scheduler; this is a controller that complements existing scheduling logic
Support for on-prem air-gapped customers in initial rollout (will follow)
constraints: Controller must add <10% CPU overhead on control-plane instances at 10k concurrent reservations
Must not require kernel-level changes or new GPU-side agents
Telemetry retention for reserve events follows existing Console retention limits unless extended
requirements: REQ-1: Soft headroom pool manager: allocate and revoke transient headroom in millisecond-to-second decision windows
REQ-2: Tenant burst budget: per-tenant configurable burst_credit (tokens) with linear decay and replenishment rules
REQ-3: Isolation enforcement: when headroom exhausted, controller triggers graceful fallback routing to allowed model variants or lower-tier capacity per policy
REQ-4: Preemption hooks: expose an API that scheduler/worker processes can call to request immediate reclaim of soft headroom
REQ-5: Operator controls: Console UI to set reserve policy, emergency reclamation toggles, and tenant exemptions
REQ-6: Telemetry: emit structured events (reserve-grant, reserve-reclaim, fallback-trigger) with tenant, reservation id, trigger cause, and latency impact
REQ-7: Auditability: record decisions for 90 days (tenant, timestamp, decision) in existing audit logs
REQ-8: Backwards compatibility: existing reserved-pool APIs remain unchanged; this controller observes existing reservation metadata
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: In a staging cluster with 500 simulated tenants, controller grants transient headroom and reclaims it within 60s with <1% false-positive preemptions
AC-2: Under mixed load, no tenant suffers >2x latency degradation over baseline if they are within their configured burst budget
AC-3: Console shows reserve activity graphs, and operators can change a tenant's burst_budget in UI and see effect within 30s
AC-4: Controller decision logic is covered by end-to-end tests; can simulate exhaustion and validate fallback routes via CI test harness
AC-5: CPU overhead measured on control-plane does not exceed 10% at target scale
success_metrics: Reduce customer-visible throttles for bursty tenants by 40% in first month post-rollout
Maintain 99.9% P95 latency SLO for dedicated tenants during normal and burst traffic
Operator mean time to identify reserve reclamation events < 5 minutes via Console dashboards
design_considerations: Use token-bucket style burst budget per tenant to keep state compact
Favor eventual consistency for non-critical telemetry to avoid control-plane stalls
Conservative default policies with opt-in aggressive modes for customers who permit higher cross-tenant sharing
Design hooks for future admission control integration with autoscaler metrics
ops_requirements: Runbook: steps to manually drain soft headroom and force preemptions
Monitoring: alerts for reserve-hit-rate > 5% over 10m and reclaim-failure-rate > 0.5%
Ability to toggle controller (on/off) per-region for quick rollback
rollout_plan: Canary: enable controller in 1 region with opt-in tenants (10 customers) for 2 weeks
Stage: expand to 30% of Dedicated capacity and run chaos tests for 1 week
GA: full region-by-region rollout with gradual ramp and operator training
Post-GA: collect telemetry and iterate on default burst budgets based on observed distributions
notes: Tradeoff: aggressive sharing reduces throttles but increases risk of noisy-neighbor events; default opts toward isolation
We will instrument per-tenant rollback thresholds to avoid oscillation
Future: integrate reserve controller with predictive warmers based on traffic forecasts
